analysis: What changed versus the 4:00 AM brief: the freshest print of the morning is Nebius — a beat that the market is selling. Q3 revenue of $980.8M (+571% YoY) topped the ~$907M consensus and adjusted EPS of -$0.13 beat the -$0.72 estimate, but CEO Volozh flagged December revenue slipping to February, pushing 2026 guidance to the low end of $3.0-3.4B; NBIS is down ~8.3% premarket to $141.90. That makes two neocloud names in two days whose strong demand prints are being met with funding/timing questions — CoreWeave gave back a chunk of its +24.7% surge with -7.2% premarket — which keeps the HN circular-financing thread (still the best community read) squarely in play. The Nvidia story is unchanged in substance but deeper in price: NVDA $160.69 (-7.51%) premarket, still no board decision, news expected later Thursday; AMD/Broadcom stay the rotation beneficiaries. The co-headline is now rates: Deutsche Bank's three-straight-hikes call (Dec/Jan/Mar to 4.50-4.75%) plus a 19-month-high dollar above 103 and the 10Y back above 5.01% as bond trading resumed — the market now prices a ~62% chance of 50bp of tightening across the next two meetings, versus 10% a week ago. Signal vs noise: the Nebius guide cut and the DB rate-path revision are signal (both are primary-source, multi-outlet); the Musk 'honor to hire Huang' chatter on HN is noise with no discussion behind it; the Polymarket 'SPX down' lean (33% up) is sentiment color, not data.

community_signals.takeaway: 182-comment thread dissecting the circular financing behind the GPU boom (Nvidia, CoreWeave, Nebius) — the funding-structure skepticism that Wednesday's CoreWeave print briefly answered, that Nebius's guide cut this morning revives, and that today's Nvidia leadership shock puts back on the table.

headlines.headline: Nebius (NBIS) beat Q3 estimates but tumbled ~8.3% premarket to $141.90: revenue $980.8M (+571% YoY) vs ~$907M expected, adjusted EPS -$0.13 vs -$0.72 expected, adjusted EBITDA $465.8M (47% margin), and a 2027 sales outlook of $12-13B. But CEO Arkady Volozh said December revenue will likely slip to February, pushing 2026 revenue to the low end of the $3.0-3.4B range. Prepayments covered more than 100% of Q3 capex tied to those contracts. The earnings call starts at 8:00 AM ET (5:00 AM PT). NBIS closed Wednesday at $154.69 (+15.44%).
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat sold off on timing, not demand — the second neocloud name in two days whose strong print met funding/timing skepticism, so the guide, not the revenue beat, sets the tone for AI-infrastructure names into the open.

headlines.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) is down about 7.5% premarket to ~$160.69, still with no board decision announced on CEO Jensen Huang's future; news is expected later Thursday. The board met Wednesday night; the WSJ reported it is preparing to oust Huang after the NYT reported a second extramarital relationship, this one with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. The chip split persists: AMD and Broadcom each up 3%+ premarket, while Intel, Marvell and Micron fell 2.6-3.4% and CoreWeave fell 7.2%. NVDA closed Wednesday at $173.73 (+2.87%); NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17.
headlines.why_it_matters: The -7.5% move still prices uncertainty, not a done deal — any board statement later today is the swing factor for NVDA and the whole AI complex.

headlines.why_it_matters: Wednesday's CoreWeave-led rally is giving back its tech half overnight while the Dow holds flat — the rotation shape continues, with the Nvidia headline doing the damage rather than broad selling.

headlines.headline: Deutsche Bank now expects three straight Fed hikes — 25bp in December, January and March — lifting the funds rate to 4.50-4.75%, after October CPI ran hot (+0.4% MoM vs +0.3% expected). It does not rule out a 50bp December move but that is not its base case. CME FedWatch now puts a ~62% chance on 50bp of tightening across the next two meetings, versus 10% a week ago; a December 25bp hike is priced at ~91%. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.01% (+~2bp) as bond trading resumed after Veterans Day; the 2-year is 4.78% (+5bp) and the 30-year steady at 5.35%. The dollar index is above 103, a fresh 19-month high. Five Fed speakers are on today's docket, including New York Fed President John Williams, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Governor Michael Barr.
headlines.why_it_matters: The debate has moved from whether December happens to how far the tightening runs — a three-hike path plus a 19-month-high dollar is a headwind for growth stocks on top of the Nvidia governance shock.

Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.1M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, ~$0.03 beat), the $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M, and the J-W Power acquisition closed (~$860M, adding 0.8M+ horsepower for a combined fleet of ~4.4M, ~5M at quarter end).
